question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-3x(t)+9y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-x(t)+3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector corresponding to the only eigenvalue $\lambda=0$ of the system's matrix $A$ is $\mathbf{v} = [3, \ 1]^T.$ The vector $\mathbf{w} = [-1, \ 0]^T$ is such that $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$  Sketch the phase portrait of the system.
question.worked_solution:
Since we have a repeated eigenvalue $\lambda=0$ (of multiplicity two) and only one corresponding eigenvector $\mathbf{v},$ the solution of the system is given by

$$
\mathbf{x}(t) = c_1\mathbf{v} e^{\lambda t}  + c_2 (\mathbf{v}  te^{\lambda t}  +  \mathbf{w}e^{\lambda t} \, ),
$$

where $\mathbf{w}$ is a solution to the equation $(A - \lambda I)\mathbf{w}= \mathbf{v}.$

In our case, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130948/assets/b0b5abdfe48d45a352b101e134ebb06165824385c1162a705e539f911af9f267.svg) 
Thus, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]t+[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3t-1 \\ t\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

First, notice that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130948/assets/962887c2e859c2afadfc122bd5ecc22fe28eb354b348c5153c16577de5fe37d8.svg) are equilibrium solutions of the system since $\mathbf{x}'_E(t) = \mathbf{0}.$ These solutions form the line with the equation $y=\dfrac13x$ in the phase space, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130948/assets/bfc7b00f7f63aec120179da3f89f72f0aa53f13d299c95ed8f53e6238d329e51.png)

Now, we consider some general solutions of the form 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130948/assets/9bbb4470407c8498cf3270e247e7b9a9d214bd1ff1b3d85a75d17189bee26ea9.svg)
For example:

- When $c_1=1$ and $c_2=1,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=3t+2 \\ y=t+1\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130948/assets/55dfdfce480deba74fe46c1634e4c7ffb711fbd617525cdb5387bdabfc83ae75.png)

- When $c_1=-1$ and $c_2=-1,$ we get the following curve: 

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-3t-2 \\ y=-t-1\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add it to the phase space:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130948/assets/2fb2297c741ea20ca729dcacb9934d7f8d1cca58af93c2b75db177890934b2b6.png)

The phase portrait of our system looks as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14130948/assets/9e7970ba2d6bbe4745ee498cdbc72f2b7d8689219291847644bd6483696cc456.png)
